_meta: Close the refuter-economics gap surfaced by a downstream transcript: three refutations ran ~540k tokens on the session's strongest model because (a) the INTERACTIVE surface has no machine-readable model binding at all — profile.model reaches the exec dispatch (T147), but the composed refute prompt carries NO model line (the `model:` serialization exists only in a profile's SKILL.md rendering; round-1 refutation corrected this premise), so an interactive host has nothing to act on and refuters inherit the parent model; (b) review events record reviewer/artifact/citations but NOT which model reviewed, so 'is the cheaper refuter catching as much?' is unanswerable from the log; (c) no how-to frames model tiering — cross-model-verification.md argues capability DIVERSITY (correctness), not economy, and the honest limit (cheaper is not automatically differently-failing) is undocumented. Three phases: RE1 closes the interactive last mile (`hb refute-prompt --json` emitting {prompt, model, provider, panel, refute_if} + skill/PROTOCOL review_pending text instructing the host BOTH halves: SPAWN the refuter on the profile's model, and RECORD the verdict with `hb review … --model <that model>` — the TEXT compose stays byte-identical, protecting the T147 byte-parity contract); RE2 records model provenance on review events (exec path auto-stamps the resolved profile.model / HB_REFUTE_MODEL; interactive AND MCP get a `model` argument — mcp_server's review tool schema included; review FAIL events carry it too; absent model recorded as null, never fabricated) and extends refuter-impact with a per-model catch/cleared breakdown — the repo's chosen HONEST measurement, catches-from-truth, extended with the capability axis; RE3 ships the gated how-to (tier by review KIND: plan refutation stays strong, gate-checklist reviews may go cheap — with an honest-limit section covering: cheaper ≠ differently-failing, watch per-model impact before trusting a downgrade, never downgrade to buy a pass, and the TRUST BOUNDARY of the field itself: an interactive/MCP `--model` is the recording actor's self-report while only the exec auto-stamp is config-derived). Deliberately deferred, so the limit is loud: interactive panel FAN-OUT (--json emits panel+refute_if so a host CAN aggregate, but instructing N spawns is out of scope this wave) and `audit --agent` model routing (plan refutation stays on the strong model by convention; no mechanism yet — its spend stays outside the impact report). Constraints held throughout: node ≡ python on every shared surface (compose --json, review event shape, impact summary — each gets a parity case, with a fixture MIXING null and named models to pin the null-key serialization trap), review-artifact Sev-1 rot checks and the four review-pass guards are untouched, no new audit rule. Dogfood, wired not claimed: this project's .hb/refuters/correctness.json binds model 'sonnet' (plan prep, done before RE1 runs), so GATE_RE1/RE2 reviews route cheap, while GATE_RE3's default profile stays unbound and inherits the strong session model — the tiering itself, and the plan-level refutation ran strong (round 1: UNSOUND, 2 blocking + 9 weakening findings, all folded in; artifact in .hb/reviews/).

phases.title: Gated how-to: tier the refuter (economy without weakening the adversary)

tasks.title: Author docs/howto/tier-the-refuter.md claiming only what the proofs show
tasks.description: The guide: profiles are the economic dial — bind model per refuter profile (`"model": "sonnet"` in .hb/refuters/<name>.json), reaching BOTH the exec dispatch (T147) and, via refute-prompt --json + the skill instruction, the interactive spawn (RE1's proof). Route by review KIND: plan refutation (audit --agent, design reading) stays on the strong model; gate-checklist reviews (explicit brief, grep-and-report) may go cheap. Verify the routing took effect — observe the review event's model field (RE2), do not guess. MUST contain an 'Honest limit' section covering FOUR limits: cheaper is not automatically differently-failing — a downgraded refuter can be a subset-failing one; watch the per-model impact report (catches from truth; misses invisible by definition) before trusting a downgrade; never downgrade to make a pass cheaper to obtain; and the field's trust boundary — an interactive/MCP --model is the recording actor's SELF-REPORT while only the exec auto-stamp is config-derived, so per-model impact from interactive runs is bookkeeping, not evidence. Also state the deliberate deferrals (interactive panel fan-out; audit --agent routing — plan-refutation spend stays outside the impact report). Cross-link cross-model-verification.md (capability diversity) and spend-the-model-only-on-work.md (when, not which).
